title: FREE 4 days split for intermediates (Upper Lower Fullbody Fullbody)
summary: NH designs live, thinking aloud, a 4-day upper/lower/full body/full body program for a subscriber training Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday, with Sunday as a GPP fallback. He leans on heavy compound lifts (4-8 reps) followed by lighter variations supersetted with chin-ups/pull-ups, plus finisher circuits for abs, calves, grip and rear delts. He explains choices like making lower day squat-focused, keeping upper days longer but lower days more intense, and avoiding a Sunday full body before Monday upper.

claims.claim: When a client says a certain template 'would be best', it is usually a covert request, so he follows their preferred structure.
For a schedule of Monday, Tuesday, Thursday plus Saturday or Sunday, he uses Monday upper, Tuesday lower, Thursday full body and Saturday full body.
A full body session on Sunday would compromise a hard Monday upper day, so if Saturday is missed, Sunday becomes a GPP day instead.
Start an upper day with a compound lift that recruits the most muscle; bench or dips involve more muscle than overhead press, so start with one of those.
Main lifts (bench/dips, OHP, squat, deadlift, weighted pull-ups) are done for 4-8 reps, 3-5 sets; variations for 6-10 or 8-12 reps, 4 sets; reps and sets are suggestions to adapt.
Choose bench or dips based on what agrees with you; that choice determines the follow-up variation (close-grip bench or paused dips).
Close-grip bench doesn't tax the shoulder much; both close-grip bench and mid-way paused dips shift work to the triceps and are done with less weight.
Upper/lower templates give poor upper back frequency, so he supersets chin-ups with pressing variations; chin-ups don't tax the chest and build work capacity.
If you only train four days a week you should work hard, using supersets and giant sets.
Skullcrushers are added to target the long head of the triceps, which pressing doesn't fully work.
Pendlay rows supersetted with barbell shrugs and skullcrushers; in a crowded gym, swap Pendlay rows for seal rows to reuse the bench.
Pre-fatiguing biceps with curls does not really hurt chin-up performance since chin-ups are mostly upper back; he supersets heavy curls with chin-ups himself.
Optional upper-day finisher: an ongoing circuit of abs, face pulls (10-15 reps) and lateral raises (8-12 reps) if you have 10 minutes and energy left.
He dislikes upper/lower splits because lower days force you to cram squats and deadlifts together, which is too much; upper days are fine since bench and OHP complement each other.
The lower day is squat-heavy: a heavy squat variation of choice (low bar, high bar, front, SSB) done as heavy as possible, then a lighter higher-volume squat variation supersetted with pull-ups.
You can never do too much pull-ups.
No leg extensions are needed; squats take care of the quads and glutes.
For hamstrings after squats, pick RDLs, stiff-legged deadlifts or hyperextensions depending on how strong your lower back is; he says his lower back is bulletproof.
Barbell hyperextensions are the least taxing on the lower back but learn bodyweight, then dumbbell/plate versions before loading a barbell, or it can be dangerous.
Grip work on lower day: Coan grip, plate or dumbbell holds with arms fully extended for 15 s, which strengthens forearms without taxing elbow flexors tired from upper day.
Compound movements smoke glutes, hamstrings and lower back so no isolation is needed; he never isolated hip musculature and never had issues.
Finishing with pull-ups decompresses the spine after heavy lower body work.
Upper body days should be longer with more volume; lower body days shorter but more intense because you move more weight, leaving you more tired.
After the lower day, two full rest days are needed before the Thursday full body.
He is not a big fan of full body workouts; hitting the whole body in one day doesn't seem smart to him.

Thursday full body: heavy deadlift variation from the floor (sumo, conventional, trap bar), squat variation + pull-ups, heavy bench or dips, accessory press + skullcrushers, then weighted pull-ups or rows + chin-ups, finishing with abs, calves and grip.
For lifters with a fried lower back, choose weighted pull-ups over Pendlay or Coan rows after deadlifts.
Saturday full body mirrors Thursday but starts with heavy squat followed by a deadlift variation.
If you can't bench or dip heavy on Monday, Thursday and Saturday, replace the heavy pressing with the accessories plus high-volume push-ups at the end.
GPP is context based: swim, run or do sport; for lifting, do high-volume pull-ups, push-ups, ab work, plate carries, trap work and bodyweight hyperextensions that won't fry you for the next session.
